title: Find a word in a letter grid
summary: Trace a word letter by letter through a grid, chalking each square as you go and rubbing the mark out when a path fails.
goal: Decide whether the word can be traced through neighbouring squares

mapping.formal: A path of adjacent cells spelling it
Marking a cell as used on this path

examples.label: ABCCED
examples.explanation: A-B-C along the top, down to C, then E and D.

examples.label: SEE
examples.explanation: S on the right edge, then down to E and E.

examples.label: ABCB
examples.explanation: The path would need the B square twice.

ladder.name: List every path of the right length
ladder.idea: From every square, list every path of the word's length that never reuses a square, then compare each path's letters with the word.

ladder.name: Trace letter by letter, give up early
ladder.idea: From each square matching the first letter, step to a neighbour matching the next letter, chalking squares on the way. Rub the chalk out when a path fails.
ladder.insight: A path that already spells the wrong letter can never become right, so stop it immediately instead of building it to full length.
ladder.time: O(m·n·4ᴸ) worst case, usually far less

transfer.problem: On a word-game board, check whether a player's word can be formed from touching tiles, using each tile once.
transfer.explanation: Trace the word from each starting tile, marking used tiles and unmarking them when a path fails.

selfCheck: Stops a path as soon as a letter does not match.
Marks a square before exploring from it and unmarks it after.
Moves only up, down, left and right.
Tries every square as a starting point.
